description: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger is represented at 14.9%, and Sadness at 14.7%, with both categories shown in distinct yellow and orange slices. Excitement accounts for 14.1%, and Happiness is the smallest category at 8.1%. The chart uses a clear color-coded scheme with labels positioned outside each slice for readability, and the segments are arranged in a clockwise sequence starting from Frustration. The visual representation highlights a relatively balanced distribution among negative emotions, with positive emotions being less prevalent.

Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.
